title: Kingdom of Sophene
capsule: The Kingdom of Sophene (Armenian: Ծոփքի թագավորություն) was a Hellenistic polity in the upper Euphrates region, corresponding roughly to the area around modern Elazığ in eastern Turkey, ruled by a branch of the Iranian-origin Orontid dynasty from at least the mid-3rd century BCE with capitals at Arsamosata and Carcathiocerta. It maintained semi-independent status as a buffer between the Seleucid Empire and Greater Armenia, its rulers combining Zoroastrian religious practice with Hellenistic coinage and Greek-language decrees. Around 95 BCE Tigranes the Great of the Artaxiad dynasty conquered Sophene; Rome reorganized the region following Lucullus's and Pompey's campaigns (74–66 BCE), and the territory subsequently passed among Roman, Parthian, and Armenian jurisdictions before being definitively absorbed as an Armenian province, with Trajan briefly establishing a Roman province of Armenia in 114 CE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Sophene's territory is reasonably attested in ancient sources as a distinct region but its precise administrative borders at any given moment are inferential, reconstructed from fragmentary Hellenistic and Armenian historiography.
